proposals.evidence: Probable regional loan, but inherited edible-root vocabulary with a later semantic extension remains an alternative. Turner1388 section1 includes Hindi/Punjabi ālū potato alongside older ālu edible-root senses; it does not explicitly attest Dameli. The Khowar dictionary independently gives alú potato (p4), and compiled Pashto f_okjicf5lkel6g gives ālū potato. These establish the regional family without selecting Urdu, Pashto or Khowar as the immediate donor. Do not conflate Turner1389 fruit or Khowar aluk pumpkin with this potato sense.

proposals.evidence: Compiled Hallberg Pashto f_azfzkyoxumwka has the exact pʰalī groundnut, with palī and mūmpʰalī among other survey variants. Platts independently attests Hindustani phalī pod, establishing the broader plant-name family but not the groundnut sense or immediate borrowing route. A regional loan is plausible; retention of an inherited pod word with semantic specialization is not excluded. Do not treat the form as the unrelated ploughshare word or assert that Dameli itself shortened mūmpʰalī.

proposed_donor.language: Probable Pashto-mediated regional compound; donor unresolved

proposals.evidence: Compiled Hallberg f_bw2n765yxj7jk has Pashto gval gopī cauliflower, closely matching the complete Dameli gulgopī, rather than only its final element. Platts gobhī explicitly includes cabbage and labels its remote Sanskrit comparison uncertain; that does not prove the full compound or its ultimate origin. Pashto mediation is a plausible inference, but gul versus gval and the original survey transcription need checking. Treat this as a possible whole borrowed compound, not an established synchronic Dameli flower-plus-cabbage derivation.
